# 09 — RynthNav → holtburger-web movement integration

## 0. TL;DR

RynthNav is a **three-artifact system**: two offline C# CLI bakers (produce `.tile` navmeshes + `portals.tsv`) and one in-process C# plugin that does Detour navmesh queries + a Dijkstra portal planner + a steering servo. The web client (`holtburger-web`) **already contains a faithful retail steering machine** (`MoveToManager` in `holtburger-core`, with `move_to_position`/`move_to_object`/`turn_to_heading`), of which `pursueEntity`/`turnToHeading`/`setMovementInput`/`setAutoRun` are already exposed to JS. So the clean split is:

- **RynthNav = global router** (offline bakes + Detour-query + portal-Dijkstra) → emits an ordered list of `(NS, EW)` legs, each optionally flagged "use portal here".
- **holtburger-web = local steering executor** — its native `MoveToManager` walks each leg; RynthNav's own servo (`StepGoto`/`ApplyMovement`/`StepPortalWait`, ~230 lines) is **dropped**, not ported.

The seam is the waypoint list. The single keystone new export is `SessionHandle.moveToPosition(ns, ew, z, run)` wiring the already-present-but-crate-private `MoveToManager::move_to_position`. The Detour query itself (DotRecast, C#/win-x86) is the only piece that must be re-hosted for the browser — either as a **sidecar next to `holtburger-wsbridge`** (cheap first cut) or a **Rust/wasm Recast-Detour port** (pure-client endgame). The bakers stay offline forever; only their DAT input path changes.

## 1. RynthNav dependency graph — host calls vs DAT files vs pure math

Line counts verified by `wc -l`.

| Component | File | Lines | DotRecast dep | AC-DAT dep | Host-call dep | Pure math |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime plugin | `Plugins/RynthCore.Plugin.RynthNav/RynthNavPlugin.cs` | 754 | **Detour (query)** | none at runtime (reads baked `.tile`/`.tsv` from disk) | **12 distinct Host.\* methods** | tile-window streaming, replan cadence, arrival math |
| Native exports | `.../RynthNav/PluginExports.cs` | 84 | — | — | C-ABI bridge only | — |
| Portal planner | `Tools/RynthNav.PortalGraph/PortalRoute.cs` | 205 | none | none | none | **100% pure** (Dijkstra over portal endpoints) |
| Portal extractor | `Tools/RynthNav.PortalGraph/Program.cs` | 230 | none | none (reads vendored `GAlocations.xml`) | none | XML→TSV/JSON transform |
| Navmesh baker | `Tools/RynthNav.Baker/NavBake.cs` | 213 | **Recast (bake) + Detour** | `RynthCore.TerrainData` + `AcClientReborn.Landblock` (`GeometryLoader`) | none (offline) | axis remap, triangulation |
| Baker CLI | `Tools/RynthNav.Baker/Program.cs` | 151 | Recast/Detour | terrain+geometry DAT readers | none | region/watch loop |
| Dungeon A* | `Plugins/RynthCore.Plugin.RynthAi/DungeonPathfinder.cs` | 741 | **none** | `DatDatabase cellDat` (EnvCell parse) | none | A*, IsDropEdge, 2-core prune, Euler walk |

### 1a. The runtime host-call surface (exhaustive)

`RynthNavPlugin.cs` touches the host through exactly **12 distinct methods, 63 call sites** (`grep -oE 'Host\.[A-Za-z]+'`):

| Host method | Call sites (line) | Purpose | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TryGetPlayerPose(cell,x,y,z,…)` | 126 | read pose each tick | TryGet reader |
| `HasGetPlayerPose` | 125 | capability guard | Has* guard |
| `SetAutoRun(bool)` | 364,377,388,390,397,430,445,496,515,538,545,546 | forward run drive | fire-and-forget |
| `DoMovement(motion,speed,hold)` | 391,398 | backward walk drive | fire-and-forget |
| `StopMovement(motion,hold)` | 365,378,389 | stop a drive | fire-and-forget |
| `SetMotion(motion,bool)` | 366,367,379,380,403–406 | turn-left/right holds | fire-and-forget |
| `StopCompletely()` | 368,381,496,515,546 | full halt | fire-and-forget |
| `TurnToHeading(float deg)` | 444,537 | steer toward waypoint | fire-and-forget |
| `IsPortaling()` / `HasIsPortaling` | 507 | teleport-in-progress signal | TryGet reader |
| `WriteToChat` / `Log` | many | UI/log | side-channel |

**Every one of these is a movement primitive or a pose read** — RynthNav is a thin actuator over the host's steering, exactly matching Doc `MeshNav_DeepDive`'s "no AC mutation beyond the existing safe primitives" stability story (`MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:94`). This is why the servo is disposable on web: the web client owns better versions of all of them.

### 1b. Dungeon pathfinder — verified pure C# except DAT read

`DungeonPathfinder.cs` is **algorithmically pure** (A* `FindPath:275`, `IsDropEdge:61`, 2-core patrol prune `GetMainRouteNodes:451`, Euler closed-walk `BuildPatrolRoute:530`). Its only external couplings:
- **Input:** `DatDatabase cellDat` — reads EnvCell binary directly (`cellDat.GetLandblockCellIds`, `cellDat.GetFileData`, `DungeonPathfinder.cs:122–125`) and hand-parses the EnvCell header for portal-record adjacency (`:151–167`). This is a **cell.dat read**, not a host call.
- **Output:** builds `NavRouteParser`/`NavPoint` (RynthAi types, `:353–372`).
- **Known limitation (carried from Nav deep-dive J3):** `IsDropEdge` prunes *all* jump/drop edges (`:262,306`), so drop-gated dungeon areas are unreachable (`Nav_DeepDive_2026-06-15.md:164`).

Crucially, the web client **already builds this exact graph** for rendering: `getRenderSet(depth)` is a BFS over EnvCell portal neighbors (`lib.rs:30434`), and the EnvCell reader exposes `portal_cell_id_count()`/`take_portal_cell_ids()` (`lib.rs:15962,15975`) plus `getCurrentCellId()` (`lib.rs:30420`) and `isCurrentCellIndoor()` (`lib.rs:31069`). So on web, DungeonPathfinder's `BuildGraph` DAT-read is **replaced by web-client cell data**; only the pure A*/patrol layer needs to move.

## 2. Data artifacts

### 2a. Navmesh `.tile` format
- **One Detour tile per AC landblock** (192 m square). Serialized with `DtMeshDataWriter().Write(bw, md, LITTLE_ENDIAN, false)` (`NavBake.cs:184–189`), read back with `DtMeshDataReader().Read(br, VertsPerPoly)` (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:160`).
- **Filename:** `nav_{lb:X4}.tile` in `C:\Games\RynthCore\NavData` (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:30,155`; `NavBake.cs:104,150`).
- **Bake params** (`NavBake.cs:26,72–84`): `VertsPerPoly=6`, tiled `cellSize=0.5`, `tileSize=384` (384×0.5 = 192 m), `cellHeight=0.20`, `agentHeight=2.0`, `agentRadius≈2.0`, `agentMaxClimb=1.0`, `agentMaxSlope=acos(FloorZ)`, WATERSHED partitioning.
- **Axis remap** AC(Z-up: x=EW, y=NS, z=height) → Recast(Y-up): `AcToRec(ewX,nsY,upZ) = (ewX, upZ, nsY)` (`NavBake.cs:28`). Tiled tiles rewrite their header `x`/`y` to **absolute landblock coords** so the plugin streams a window that reconnects (`NavBake.cs:135–150`).
- **Geometry sources:** terrain 9×9 grid triangulated with the AC diagonal-split PRNG `TerrainSampler.SwToNeCut` (`NavBake.cs:41–50`) + static objects/scatter from `GeometryLoader.GetTexturedStaticObjects`/`GetTexturedScatter` (`:64–65`). Dungeon walls (`DungeonLOS`) are a *planned* later phase, not yet baked (`MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:80,104`).
- **Status:** Phase 0 proven — Holtburg `0xA9B4` → 265 polys, `.tile` round-trips (`MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:101`).

### 2b. `portals.tsv` schema (817 rows verified)
Tab-separated, no header, **5 columns** (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:562–568`; emitted `Program.cs:127–138`):

| col | field | example |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `SrcNs` | `26.3` |
| 1 | `SrcEw` | `63.9` |
| 2 | `DstNs` | `-65.9` |
| 3 | `DstEw` | `59.7` |
| 4 | `Name` (optional) | `Merchant Cellar to High Mountain Valley` |

Coords are **AC /loc decimal degrees**; a row is a directed edge "walk to Src → teleport → arrive Dst". **817 edges** from 5,258 GoArrow locations (`PortalGraph/README.md:33`). **Gotcha:** GoArrow stores North as *negative* latitude; the extractor negates it (`Program.cs:80–83`). This is **retail data on an ACE server** — README warns to validate empirically; arrival coords rounded to ~0.1° (`README.md:16–18`). `portals.json` carries the richer schema (Id, Type, Restrictions, PkRequired — `Program.cs:214–230`); the AOT plugin reads only the TSV to avoid a JSON-reflection dependency (`README.md:66–70`).

### 2c. Portal planner (`PortalRoute.Plan`)
Uniform-cost Dijkstra over `{START, GOAL, per-portal (Src,Dst) pairs, recall dsts}` (`PortalRoute.cs:71–204`). Tunables: `PortalPenaltyUnits=360`, `RecallPenaltyUnits=1200`, `ChainWalkRadiusUnits=4000`, `UnitsPerDegree=240` (`:45–54`). Returns `List<RouteStep>{Ns,Ew,UsePortal,UseRecall,Label}` (`:33–41`). **Compiled into both the offline tool and the plugin** via `<Compile Include>` so validated == shipped (`RynthCore.Plugin.RynthNav.csproj` links `PortalRoute.cs`; `README.md:52–54`).

### 3b. The pose coordinate frame — bridges cleanly to RynthNav
`LocalPlayerPose { x, y, z, heading, landblock_id, on_ground }` (`lib.rs:28849`), populated from `world.local_player_runtime_pose()` at `lib.rs:36804`:
- `x/y/z = pose.coords.{x,y,z}` are **landblock-local meters** (0..192), `landblock_id` separate (`:36805–36809`).
- `heading` is Z-up yaw in **radians**, `0 = +Y = North`, `+π/2 = +X = East`, extracted `atan2(2(qw·qz+qx·qy), 1−2(qy²+qz²))` (`:36801–36803`).

RynthNav's world frame is `worldEW = lbX*192 + local.x`, `worldNS = lbY*192 + local.y`, `/loc EW=(worldEW/24−1019.5)/10` (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:129,585–586,707`). Given web `landblock_id` → `lbX=(id>>24)&0xFF`, `lbY=(id>>16)&0xFF` (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:128`) plus `coords.x/y`, the router **reconstructs RynthNav's exact NS/EW with the same formula** — the frames are identical modulo the lb-local vs absolute offset the router already applies. Heading basis matches (both put N=0, E=+90°); only unit differs (web radians vs RynthNav degrees), and `turnToHeading` already takes radians — but the router won't usually supply heading, since MoveToManager steers itself.

### 3c. The MoveTo steering machine (the executor)
`crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/move_to.rs` is a faithful port of retail `MoveToManager` (`move_to.rs:127,306`). It has:
- `move_to_object(target, params)` — `move_to.rs:509` (retail 345184)
- **`move_to_position(origin, params)` — `move_to.rs:530` (retail HandleMoveToPosition 345790)** ← the target-a-coordinate driver, **crate-private, not yet reachable from JS**
- `turn_to_object` `:544`, `turn_to_heading` `:562`.

Drive intents flow JS → `SessionCommand` → recv-loop → `movement.enqueue_drive_intent(PlayerDriveIntent::…)` (`lib.rs:46597`). `PlayerDriveIntent` (`movement_types.rs:184`) has `ManualHeld`, `ManualPulse`, `Autonomous(AutonomousDriveIntent)`, **`ArriveAtPose{pose}`**, `SnapFacing`, `Stop`, `PursueObject`, `TurnToObject`, `TurnToHeading`, `CancelPursuit`. There is **no `MoveToPosition` intent** and **no `ArriveAtPose` JS export** — `ArriveAtPose` routes to `QueuedDriveCommand::ArriveAtPose` (`system.rs:2741,2884`) but nothing calls it from the command channel. That is the exact gap to fill.

### 3d. Keyboard-walk path
`index.html` funnels the WASD/camera dispatcher through **one shared `setMovementInput` boundary** (`index.html:1397,6149,6234`), computing `(forward, strafe, turn, run)` then calling `handle.setMovementInput(forward,strafe,turn,run)` (`index.html:9232`, logged `:9236`). Autorun is a typeof-guarded `handle.setAutoRun(on)` under `?retailRunKeys` (`index.html:6512–6532`). Pose read for JS is `window.getLocalPlayerPose = () => window.__sessionHandle?.getLocalPlayerPose?.()` (`index.html:1432`).

### 3e. Teleport is server-authoritative (no client teleport)
There is **no client-side teleport export** and **no `IsPortaling`/teleport-sequence getter** exposed to JS (grep: none). The k1 bot "teleports" via a **GM chat command** `sendChat("@telepoi holtburg")` (`k1_drive_combat.cjs:196`), i.e. the server moves the player. Portals fire server-side on collision/use; the client observes a `PlayerTeleport`/`teleport_sequence` event (`lib.rs:21175–21176`) that overwrites the local pose. **Implication:** RynthNav's `IsPortaling()` trigger has no JS twin — but its *reliable* trigger is a **landblock change** (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:509,511`), and the web pose exposes `landblockId`, so the router detects portal completion itself with zero new exports.

## (a) Component × portability table

| RynthNav component | Lines | Portability to holtburger-web | Verdict / where it lands |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PortalRoute.cs` (Dijkstra) | 205 | **Trivial** — dependency-free pure math | Reimplement in Rust (~200 lines) **or** run in sidecar as-is |
| `portals.tsv` / `portals.json` data | 817 rows | **Portable as data** (coords only) | Ship as web asset / sidecar file; re-validate vs our server |
| `PortalGraph/Program.cs` (extractor) | 230 | **Stays offline** (XML→TSV) | Run once on build box; unchanged |
| `NavBake.cs` + baker CLI | 364 | **Stays offline**; DotRecast **Recast** + AC-DAT readers | Run against our DATs on build box; output artifacts to web/sidecar |
| DungeonPathfinder A*/patrol (algorithm) | ~600 of 741 | **Portable** (pure); DAT-read layer replaced by web cell data | Reimplement A*/IsDropEdge/patrol in Rust over `getRenderSet`/EnvCell portals |
| DungeonPathfinder `BuildGraph` (DAT read) | ~90 of 741 | **Not ported** — web client already has the cell graph | Use `takePortalCellIds`/`getRenderSet` |
| RynthNav Detour **query** (EnsureTile/Replan/FindPath/FindStraightPath/string-pull) | ~150 of 754 | **Re-host required** — DotRecast.Detour is C#/win-x86 | Sidecar (.NET service reusing this code) **or** Rust/wasm Detour port |
| RynthNav **steering servo** (StepGoto/ApplyMovement/StepPortalWait) | ~230 of 754 | **Dropped** — web `MoveToManager` supersedes it | Not ported |
| RynthNav tick/threading/panel/chat plumbing | ~200 of 754 | **Dropped/rewritten** — browser is async | Replaced by JS orchestration loop |

**Portable brain: the router = Detour query (~150 lines re-hosted) + portal Dijkstra (~205 lines pure) + dungeon A* (~600 lines pure).** Disposable: the ~430 lines of servo + tick/thread/panel plumbing, because the web client already does steering natively and asynchronously.

## (b) Integration design — RynthNav as global router, web client as local steering executor

### Where the seam sits
The seam is a **waypoint contract**: the router produces an ordered `[{ns, ew, z, usePortal, label}]` list; the web client executes each leg with its native `MoveToManager`, and JS advances the leg pointer on arrival. This mirrors the doc's own "three tiers" (`MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:19–25`): RynthNav supplies **tiers 2+3 (regional pathfinding + global portal routing)**; the web client supplies **tier 1 (local steering)** — the tier the doc calls "✅ solid" and out-of-scope.

```
  OFFLINE (build box, unchanged)              RUNTIME (web session)
  ┌───────────────────┐  .tile ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ RynthNav.Baker     │──────► │ ROUTER                             │
  │ (Recast+DAT)       │        │  Detour query (findPath+string-pull│
  ├───────────────────┤ portals│  Dijkstra portal plan (PortalRoute)│──legs──►┐
  │ RynthNav.PortalGraph│──.tsv─►│  dungeon A* (over web cell graph)  │         │
  └───────────────────┘        │  hosted as SIDECAR or WASM          │◄─pose───┤
                               └────────────────────────────────────┘         │
                                                                     ┌─────────▼──────────┐
                                                                     │ holtburger-web JS   │
                                                                     │ per leg:            │
                                                                     │  moveToPosition(ns, │
                                                                     │    ew,z,run)        │
                                                                     │  poll pursuitStatus │
                                                                     │  + getLocalPlayerPose│
                                                                     │  lb-change=portal ok│
                                                                     │  MoveToManager steers│
                                                                     └─────────────────────┘
```

### Where the router physically runs — two options
| | **Option A: sidecar** (recommended first cut) | **Option B: Rust/wasm Detour** (endgame) |
|---|---|---|
| Host | A process beside `holtburger-wsbridge` (every web session already rides the bridge) | Recast-Detour port compiled into the wasm crate |
| Detour code | **Reuse the existing C# query verbatim** (or a small .NET service) | New Rust dependency (`recastnavigation` FFI is out; needs a wasm-safe port) |
| Transport | Browser ⇄ sidecar over WS/HTTP: `route(from,to) → legs` | In-process wasm call, zero network |
| Fits | `?nullRender=1` bot mode, headless CI | Pure client, offline, no extra infra |
| Effort | **Low** — no algorithm rewrite | **High** — port Recast tile query to wasm32 |
| Risk | network hop; sidecar deploy | DotRecast has no wasm target today |

Option A also honors RynthSuite's hard-won constraint *"out-of-process tooling preferred; runtime only loads cheap data"* (`MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:122`) and sidesteps the **poll-vs-async inversion** entirely: the async JS loop calls the router request/response style, so the router never needs a synchronous host-pumped tick.

### New `SessionHandle` methods needed
| New export | Wiring | Why | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`moveToPosition(ns, ew, z, run)`** (keystone) | new `SessionCommand::MoveToPosition` → new `PlayerDriveIntent::MoveToPosition` → existing `MoveToManager::move_to_position` (`move_to.rs:530`). Convert NS/EW→landblock-local `Origin`. | Run-to-a-coordinate. The one missing verb. `move_to_position` already exists & is tested (`move_to.rs:1315,1327`). | **S–M** |
| `pursuitStatus()` reuse | already exists (`lib.rs:31320`) | arrival/failure for each leg — **no new work** | — |
| `getLocalPlayerPose()` reuse | already exists (`lib.rs:31268`) | per-tick progress + **landblock-change portal-confirm** | — |
| `getCurrentCellId()` / `isCurrentCellIndoor()` / `takePortalCellIds()` reuse | exist (`lib.rs:30420,31069,15975`) | **current-cell query** for indoor A* — no new work | — |
| *(optional)* `teleportSequence()` getter | expose the existing `teleport_sequence` shadow (`lib.rs:21175`) | deterministic portal-fired signal (nicer than lb-change heuristic) | **S** |
| *(optional)* `runToObject` = `pursueEntity` reuse | exists (`lib.rs:32507`) | walk onto/into a portal *object* if walk-in coords are off (closes Nav deep-dive P3) | — |
| *(optional, portal-click)* `useObject(guid)` reuse | exists (`lib.rs:32038`) | click portals that need a use (Nav deep-dive P2/P3) | — |

**Answering the task's two explicit questions:** *run-to-position?* — yes, one new export `moveToPosition`, everything downstream already exists. *current-cell query?* — **already exposed** (`getCurrentCellId`, `isCurrentCellIndoor`, `takePortalCellIds`, `getRenderSet`); no new export needed.

### The JS orchestration loop (replaces RynthNav's `OnTick`/`StepGoto`)
```
legs = await router.route(pose→/loc, goalNs, goalEw)      // sidecar or wasm
for leg in legs:
    handle.moveToPosition(leg.ns, leg.ew, leg.z, run=true)
    await until pursuitStatus()==2 (arrived) OR pose.landblockId changed (portal fired)
    if leg.usePortal: wait for landblockId change (server teleport), then re-route from new pose
    if pursuitStatus()==3 (failed): re-plan or abort
```
This is the async analog of `RynthNavPlugin.StepGoto`/`OnSubGoalReached`/`StepPortalWait` (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:411,450,505`) — but the per-waypoint steering (`TurnToHeading`+`SetAutoRun`+arrival) is delegated to `MoveToManager`, so ~230 lines of servo evaporate.

### Coordinate / heading bridge (design detail)
Router works in `/loc` NS/EW (its native units, `RynthNavPlugin.cs:585–586`). JS reads `getLocalPlayerPose()` → reconstruct `/loc` via `EW=((coords.x + ((lbId>>24&0xFF)*192))/24 − 1019.5)/10`, `NS` likewise (RynthNav's own formula, `RynthNavPlugin.cs:707`). `moveToPosition` takes NS/EW and converts to a landblock-local `Origin` for `MoveToManager`. Heading rarely crosses the seam (MoveToManager self-steers); if it does, web is radians / N=0 (`lib.rs:36801`), matching RynthNav's basis.

## (c) What the bakers need to run against our DATs

1. **`RynthNav.PortalGraph`** — needs **nothing from our DATs**: it reads a vendored retail `GAlocations.xml` (`PortalGraph.csproj` copies `Data/GAlocations.xml`). Its 817-edge `portals.tsv` is already server-agnostic. Only action: **re-validate the retail portal coords against our ACE server** empirically (`README.md:16`), since arrival coords are ~0.1° retail approximations that may not match our worldgen.

2. **`RynthNav.Baker`** — needs **our DAT folder**. It reads `cell.dat`/`portal.dat`/terrain via `RynthCore.TerrainData` (`TerrainSampler`) + `AcClientReborn.Landblock` (`GeometryLoader`), pointed by `--ac <dats>` (default `C:\Games\ACE\Dats`, `Program.cs:45`). Run:
   - `RynthNav.Baker --ac <our-dats> --tiled <x0,x1,y0,y1> --out <navdir>` for connected regions (`Program.cs:91–104`), or `--watch` for bake-ahead driven by `_player.txt` (`Program.cs:106–141`).
   - **Prerequisite to verify:** that our DATs are the same retail-derived ACE `cell.dat`/`portal.dat` the RynthSuite readers expect (holtburger has its *own* `holtburger-dat` crate; the baker uses RynthSuite's C# readers, so this is a **DAT-format-compatibility check**, not a code-share). If layouts match, the baker runs unchanged; if not, the terrain/geometry readers need adapting — the larger risk here than the nav code itself.
   - **Environment caveats:** baker is `net10.0` + `AcClientReborn` pulls **Silk.NET** (`Baker.csproj` comment); it's an offline win/build-box tool, fine as-is. Output path is hardcoded-ish via `--out`; retarget to the web/sidecar asset dir.
   - **Coverage gap:** dungeon walls (`DungeonLOS`) are **not yet baked** into tiles (still a planned phase, `MeshNav_DeepDive_2026-06-04.md:104`), so outdoor bakes are ready but indoor navmesh isn't — indoor routing stays on the DungeonPathfinder cell-graph path.

3. **Artifact delivery:** `.tile` files + `portals.tsv` become **web assets** (fetched by the wasm router) or **sidecar files** (Option A). Either way they are static, cacheable, baked-once (respect `?nosw=1` when iterating to bypass the service-worker cache during bring-up).

## (d) Effort estimate per component

Scale: S ≈ ≤1 day, M ≈ 2–4 days, L ≈ 1–2 weeks, XL ≈ 3+ weeks. Assumes Option A (sidecar) unless noted.

| Work item | Effort | Notes / dependency |
|---|---|---|
| **`SessionHandle.moveToPosition` export** (intent + command + handle + NS/EW→Origin) | **S–M** | Keystone; `MoveToManager::move_to_position` already exists & unit-tested (`move_to.rs:1315`). Add `PlayerDriveIntent::MoveToPosition` + recv-arm mirroring `PursueObject` (`lib.rs:46583`). |
| **JS orchestration loop** (leg-walker: moveToPosition + pursuitStatus + lb-change portal-confirm + re-plan) | **M** | Replaces `StepGoto`/`StepPortalWait`; pure JS over existing exports. |
| **Router sidecar** (host DotRecast query + PortalRoute + WS/HTTP `route()`) | **M** (Option A) | Reuse C# query + `PortalRoute.cs` verbatim; wrap in a .NET service beside `holtburger-wsbridge`. |
| **Bake our DATs** (verify DAT compat, run `--tiled` for target regions) | **S–M** | S if DATs are retail-compatible; **M–L** if terrain/geometry readers need adapting. |
| **Portal data re-validation** (retail coords vs our server) | **S** | Empirical spot-checks; may prune/adjust rows. |
| **Dungeon A* on web cell graph** (port pure A*/IsDropEdge/patrol over `getRenderSet`/`takePortalCellIds`) | **M–L** | Only if indoor routing is in scope; DAT-read layer dropped. |
| *(optional)* `teleportSequence()` getter for deterministic portal-confirm | **S** | Shadow already tracked (`lib.rs:21175`). |
| **Rust/wasm Detour port** (Option B, replaces sidecar) | **XL** | DotRecast has no wasm target; largest single lift. Defer until sidecar proves the seam. |
| **Indoor navmesh bake** (`DungeonLOS` → layered Detour tiles) | **L** | Not yet built even in RynthSuite (Phase 3 pending); needed only for indoor Detour (vs cell-graph) routing. |

**Recommended path:** `moveToPosition` (S–M) + JS loop (M) + sidecar router (M) + outdoor bake (S–M) ⇒ **outdoor goto-coord-with-portals on web in ~2 weeks**, reusing the C# router unmodified and the web client's native steering. Indoor and the wasm-native router are follow-on phases (L/XL) that don't block the first working cut.

## Notes / caveats spot-checkable
- RynthNav plugin is **NativeAOT win-x86, DotRecast.Detour query-only** (`RynthCore.Plugin.RynthNav.csproj`) — it cannot load in a browser; only its *algorithm* is portable.
- The web `MoveToManager` steering is documented as sound/out-of-scope by the authors' own review (`Nav_DeepDive_2026-06-15.md:8–10`), which is exactly why the servo is safe to drop.
- Portal-*click* (`useObject`) exists on web but RynthNav's design deliberately uses **walk-in collision** (`RynthNavPlugin.cs:505`); either works, walk-in needs no targeting data.
